replacements.text: The acceptance-criteria standard has a coverage rule that asks whether each commitment has a criterion. Another rule opened with a sentence asking the same question, so its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. The rule now asks only whether each criterion names a check. The corrected control document returned an empty report in 9 of 10 panel runs, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still objected to the planted criterion.
Ten runs per document used the same model and effort. The one remaining control objection cites a flaw present in both document versions.
The `verification-contract` rule opened with a sentence that asked the coverage rule's question. It now judges each criterion's own check and leaves the other question to coverage.
The attack skill's table now names what each reviewer reads, showing which reviewer owns each rule.

A rule in the acceptance-criteria standard opened with a sentence asking the coverage rule's question, so its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. Only 2 of 10 runs on the corrected control document returned an empty report.
